title: This was a clear test, and he passed it.
subtitle: A trial measured by how quickly he obeyed

row.title: a clear trial
sub: showing what is in the heart

then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}it was clearly a test{/idea} when he was commanded to sacrifice his son, and he hastened to do it in submission and obedience. He links it to 53:37: Ibrahim who fulfilled all that was asked.
now: A loss, a hard boss, a long wait for a child. It is easy to feel targeted. {idea}The verse names it a trial: something that shows what you are made of.{/idea} Tests are where faith becomes visible.
old: This hardship means Allah is displeased with me.
new: A hard test can be the place where my faith is shown and honored.
try: Name your current test in one sentence. Ask Allah to help you pass it well.

title: Allah ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
subtitle: What was offered was returned, with a ram in its place
then: Ibn Kathir reports the ransom was a ram, and Ibn 'Abbas said {reward}a ram which had grazed in Paradise{/reward}. A report says its horns were kept in the Ka'bah until it burned. Ibn Kathir also notes the purpose of the command was to reward Ibrahim's patience and resolve.
now: Sometimes you hand something over to Allah, a plan, a relationship, a dream job, expecting to lose it. {idea}And it comes back to you, or something better is put in its place.{/idea} What He asks for is the heart.
old: If I give this up for Allah, it is gone forever.
new: What I truly hand to Allah is never lost. He knows what to return and what to replace.
try: Think of one thing you are gripping tightly. Tell Allah today it is His to keep or return.

title: Like Nuh, Ibrahim was left a good name.
subtitle: The same honor given after the same kind of trial
then: The same words were said of Nuh in verse 78. Ibrahim lost his people and his homeland and was asked for his son. {reward}Allah left for him an honored name among those who came after.{/reward}
now: You may give up a lot for your faith: a friendship, a promotion, a place you loved. {idea}What you lose for Allah is not erased.{/idea} The verse repeats so you notice the pattern.
old: What I give up for Allah just disappears.
new: Allah turns what I give up for Him into something that lasts.
try: Remember one sacrifice you made for Allah. Thank Him for letting you make it.

title: Peace upon Ibrahim, the man thrown into fire.
subtitle: Peace given to the one who was given none by his people

picture.label: From his people, then from Allah

then: His own people built a fire for him. His father rejected him. {reward}Allah greets him with peace{/reward}, as He greeted Nuh. The surah sets this beside what his enemies wanted for him.
now: Some people in your life may never speak well of you. {idea}What Allah says about you outlasts every opinion.{/idea} His peace is the greeting worth living for.
old: I am defined by how people treat me.
new: Allah's word about me matters more than anything people say.
try: When someone hurts you today, say salam to them anyway, and ask Allah for His peace.

title: Thus We reward the good: a way out every time.
subtitle: The same promise, now proven by Ibrahim
then: This line was said after Nuh and again after Ibrahim's trial. Ibn Kathir explained it as {reward}this is how We deal with those who obey Us in things that are difficult for them; We make for them a way out.{/reward}
now: You read this and think: that was for Prophets. But the word is thus, a method. {idea}The same Lord who rescued Ibrahim sees your small act of good on a tired Tuesday.{/idea}
old: Allah's help like this was only for Prophets.
new: Allah's way of rewarding good is a pattern that includes me.
try: Do one good deed today and expect good from Allah because of it.

title: After everything, he is called simply: a believing servant.
subtitle: The Friend of Allah, summed up in one phrase
then: The same line closed Nuh's story in verse 81. Ibrahim broke idols, faced the fire, left home, and passed the hardest test. {idea}Allah sums it all up: he was one of Our believing servants.{/idea}
now: Your life will not have fire or idols in a town square. It will have a commute, a family, small temptations. {idea}The title is the same one, and it is open to you.{/idea}
old: Faith like Ibrahim's is out of my reach.
new: The core of his greatness is a title I can also work toward: believing servant.
try: Ask Allah today to write you among His believing servants.

title: After the test, more good news: Ishaq.
subtitle: A second son, a Prophet from the righteous
then: Ibn Kathir says that having given the news of Isma'il, Allah {reward}immediately follows that with the glad tidings of his brother Ishaq{/reward}. Muhammad bin Ka'b noted that Ishaq's own son was also promised, as in 11:71.
now: You gave up something for Allah and braced for emptiness. {reward}Then a new door opened{/reward}: a friend, a job, a peace you did not expect. {idea}Allah's gifts often come in pairs.{/idea}
old: Once I give something up, that is the end of the story.
new: After I give for Allah, He often adds more than I expected.
try: Write down one good thing that came to you after a loss. Thank Allah for it.

title: Blessed parents, but each descendant chooses their own way.
subtitle: A great family does not guarantee a good person
then: Allah blessed Ibrahim and Ishaq, then says plainly that among their descendants are {idea}those who do good{/idea} and {trap}those who clearly wrong themselves{/trap}. Ibn Kathir compares it to the blessing given to Nuh and those with him in 11:48.
now: Your grandfather was the imam. Your parents never missed a prayer. {trap}That is a blessing, not a pass.{/trap} {idea}Every person in a family still writes their own page.{/idea}
old: I come from a good family, so I am fine.
new: A good family is a gift. My own deeds are still mine to answer for.
try: Thank Allah for one good thing your family gave you, then do one deed of your own today.

title: Two brothers, one favor: prophethood for Musa and Harun.
subtitle: Allah's grace given to a team
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us {idea}how He blessed Musa and Harun with prophethood{/idea}. The surah moves on to the next pair of Prophets, two brothers who carried the message together.
now: Think of the sibling, cousin, or friend who stands with you in doing good. The one who wakes you for Fajr, who helps with the hard family conversation. {idea}That partnership is itself a favor from Allah.{/idea}
old: What I have in my faith I built myself.
new: Every good thing I carry, and every good partner I have, is a favor from Allah.
try: Message one person who helps you stay on the right path and thank them.

title: Saved from years of crushing oppression.
subtitle: Musa, Harun and their people rescued
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved them and the believers from {trap}the oppression of Fir'awn and his people{/trap}, who persecuted them by killing their sons and forcing them into the most menial tasks. The phrase great distress was used for Nuh too.
now: Your distress might be a controlling boss, a debt that never shrinks, a home that does not feel safe. {idea}The same words that rescued Nuh rescued Musa's people.{/idea} Ask for that rescue and take the steps you can.
old: My situation is too big for anything to change.
new: Allah has rescued people from great distress before. He can do it again.
try: Name your distress to Allah in a du'a today, then take one small practical step out of it.

title: The oppressed became the ones who prevailed.
subtitle: Help from Allah turned the weak into victors
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}ultimately caused them to prevail{/reward} over those who oppressed them. The surah was heard by a small group of persecuted Muslims in Makkah, who could not imagine winning. It was meant for them.
now: You feel like the small one in the room: the junior at work, the new one in the class, the only one trying to stay clean. {idea}Victory belongs to those Allah helps, not those who look strong.{/idea}
old: Whoever looks strongest now will win.
new: The one Allah helps is the one who prevails, however weak they look.
try: Ask Allah for help today in the one area where you feel smallest.

title: Then they were given a Book that makes things clear.
subtitle: The Tawrah, after the rescue
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}revealed to Musa the Clear and Mighty Book, which is the Tawrah{/idea}, citing 21:48 where it is called the criterion and a shining light. Rescue came first, then a Book to live by.
now: You finally got the free time, the job security, the place of your own. {idea}Freedom is not the end goal. It is room to live by guidance.{/idea} Allah gave you a clear Book too.
old: Once my problems are solved, I can relax.
new: Relief is room to follow guidance, not a break from it.
try: Use part of your next free hour to read a page of the Quran with its meaning.

title: Guided to the straight path, in words and deeds.
subtitle: Guidance that shapes what you say and do
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the straight path Musa and Harun were guided to was {idea}with regard to words and deeds{/idea}. Having the Book was not enough. They were guided to live it.
now: You know the right thing. The test is the text you send, the price you charge, the way you talk to your mother. {idea}The straight path runs through your mouth and your hands.{/idea}
old: As long as my beliefs are right, I am on the path.
new: The straight path shows up in what I say and do, not only what I believe.
try: Pick one thing you say often that you know is not right. Replace it today.

title: Like Nuh and Ibrahim, they are spoken of with honor.
subtitle: The good name left for Musa and Harun

picture.label: The same gift, a third time

then: Ibn Kathir says this means {reward}after they died they would be mentioned in good terms and spoken of highly{/reward}. It is the third time the surah uses these words, each time after a Prophet was rescued.
now: Fir'awn had palaces and an army. Musa had a staff and a brother. Ask who is mentioned with honor today. {idea}The surah keeps repeating it so the lesson sticks.{/idea}
old: Power is what makes a name last.
new: Faithfulness, not power, is what Allah makes last.
try: Think of what you would want said about you after you are gone. Do one thing toward it today.

title: Peace upon Musa and Harun, together.
subtitle: Two brothers greeted in one breath
then: After the rescue, the help, the Book and the guidance, Allah greets {reward}both brothers together with peace{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this explains the good mention left for them.
now: Siblings fight over inheritance, drift apart over a wedding, stop calling. {idea}Musa and Harun are greeted with peace in one breath.{/idea} Brothers and sisters can carry good together.
old: My sibling and I are just too different to work together.
new: Siblings who stand together for good are honored together.
try: Call or message a brother or sister today, just to say salam.
